answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Attestation. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge derived from a shared public seed, and agents peer-check answers during a dune of rolling epochs. Legitimate agents diverge freely because they hold distinct internal state; clones cannot, since identical replicas return identical answers. A velvet of cross-checks flags correlated responses, forcing attackers to maintain genuinely separate state per identity. At each summit audit, every clone costs a full independent state-maintenance budget, not one shared payload.
